name: Rylo: Live Call Captioning (formerly Nagish)
oneLine: US phone-call caption app, free through the FCC for eligible users, with free in-person captions (Live Transcribe) and a desktop app for video calls.

platforms.detail: The Rylo phone app runs on iPhone, iPad and Android phones and tablets, with an Apple Watch companion. Rylo Desktop, a separate free app for Mac and Windows, captions video calls.

deviceRequirements.detail: The App Store listing needs iOS 16.6 or later (Rylo's help centre still says iOS 15+), and the help centre says Android 9+. Rylo Desktop needs macOS 14.2 or later, or 64-bit Windows 10 or 11.

roomCaptions.detail: Live Transcribe, inside the Rylo phone app, captions speech in the room through the phone's microphone. It is free with no time limits and is not part of the FCC-funded service.

groupConversations.text: One phone on the table; conference calls
groupConversations.detail: Rylo pitches Live Transcribe for group meetings with one phone on the table, and you can show the screen to the group. The phone app also captions conference and speakerphone calls; linking several phones or mics is not described.

languages.detail: Rylo's website says 50+ and its help centre lists 53 language entries. The App Store and Google Play listings name only 6, and Rylo Desktop says 60.

offline.detail: Rylo says Live Transcribe works without Wi-Fi or mobile data. Phone-call captions and Rylo Desktop need internet, and Rylo doesn't say which languages work offline.

speakerLabels.text: Rylo Desktop; not stated in person
speakerLabels.detail: Rylo Desktop marks each line with who said it, and the homepage says calls show who is speaking, typing or pausing. Speaker labels are not mentioned for Live Transcribe.

translation.detail: No Rylo page describes translating speech into another language. Rylo says it detects when the language changes during a conversation.

saveTranscripts.detail: Call transcripts save on your device by default (you can turn this off), and Live Transcribe transcripts save automatically. Rylo can't restore deleted transcripts because they aren't on its servers.

export.detail: Call and Live Transcribe transcripts can be shared from the app (formats not stated). Rylo Desktop downloads transcripts as .txt files with the title, date and who said what.

fileUpload.detail: No Rylo page mentions transcribing an uploaded audio or video file.

summaries.detail: Rylo Desktop writes an AI summary on the computer after each captioned call, with decisions and action items. Summaries are not mentioned for the phone app or Live Transcribe.

customWords.detail: You can add names, places and jargon to a personal dictionary in the call settings.

display.detail: You can change caption size during calls, and in Live Transcribe also font weight and light or dark mode.

soundAlerts.detail: No Rylo page mentions alerts for non-speech sounds. Live Transcribe shows the current sound level.

phoneCalls.detail: Rylo captions incoming and outgoing calls and voicemail, on your existing number or a new one. You can also caption your own voice, and keep captions in a floating window while you use other apps.

videoCalls.detail: Rylo Desktop for Mac and Windows captions calls in Zoom, Teams, Google Meet, Slack Huddles, FaceTime, Discord, Webex and the browser. Rylo says no bot joins the meeting.

mediaOnDevice.detail: Captioning videos or other media playing on the device is not described. During a browser call, Rylo Desktop captions all audio from that browser.

humanCaptioners.detail: Rylo's terms say captions come from automated speech recognition, and the App Store listing says there is no human involvement.

signLanguage.detail: Rylo offers AI sign language tools, Sign Translate and an ASL Sign Dictionary in beta, as separate free tools outside the caption app.

privacy.text: Calls deleted; Live Transcribe may be kept
privacy.detail: Call audio and captions are deleted from Rylo's servers once delivered. Rylo's Live Transcribe page says transcripts are saved privately on your device, but its privacy policy says Rylo Live conversations may be recorded and stored, and its terms say Live Transcribe input may be used to train its AI.

account.text: Yes; name, DOB, last 4 of SSN
account.detail: Registration asks for your address, date of birth and the last four digits of your Social Security number, as FCC rules require; Rylo's help centre says you can't register without them, while the FCC says providers may accept other documents. Rylo Desktop also needs a free Rylo account.

availability.detail: Rylo supports the United States and its territories; its App Store listing was not found in the UK, Canada, Germany, Australia or Slovenia stores. Free international calls are possible to a listed set of countries.

freePlan.text: Free for eligible users, no limits
freePlan.detail: Phone-call captions are free for eligible deaf, hard of hearing or speech-disabled users. Live Transcribe is free with no time limits or ads, and Rylo Desktop is free with no paid features.

price.detail: No paid plan is listed and the App Store shows no in-app purchases. Rylo says people who aren't eligible may not get the service for free, and its terms allow fees outside the FCC programme.

accessibilityFunding.text: Yes, FCC (IP CTS and IP Relay)
accessibilityFunding.detail: The FCC lists Nagish, Inc. d/b/a Rylo with full IP CTS and conditional IP Relay certification. Calls are paid from the federal TRS Fund, and you self-certify a hearing or speech disability.

strengths.text: Phone-call captions are free for eligible US users, and Live Transcribe and Rylo Desktop are free with no paid features.
One app covers phone calls, voicemail and in-person speech (Live Transcribe), which Rylo says also works offline.
Rylo Desktop captions Zoom, Teams, Meet and FaceTime on Mac and Windows, with speaker labels and summaries made on the computer.
Call transcripts are stored only on your device, and the content of FCC-funded calls is not kept after the call.

limits.text: Only offered in the United States and its territories, and registration needs US details including the last four digits of an SSN.
Captions are automatic only; there is no human captioner option.
Rylo's terms say Live Transcribe input may be used to train its AI, and its privacy policy says Rylo Live conversations may be recorded and stored.
Language counts differ: the store listings name 6 languages, the website says 50+, Rylo Desktop says 60.

sources.title: Is Rylo free?
quotes: Rylo is 100% free for people who are Deaf, hard of hearing, or challenged with speech.
Rylo is certified by the FCC, which means the FCC reimburses Rylo for the cost of providing its IP CTS and IP Relay services.

Rylo may offer additional services at no cost as part of our mission to make communication accessible for all, such as text-to-speech and Rylo live. These services will be offered on a case-by-case basis and are not certified or reimbursed by the FCC.

quotes: HTTP/2 301, location: https://rylo.com/ (seen 2026-10-28)

notes: Nagish has been renamed Rylo: nagish.com answers with a 301 redirect to https://rylo.com/ (s35, seen 2026-10-28), rylo.com's structured data gives legalName "Nagish Inc. dba Rylo" and alternateName "Nagish", the FCC provider list says "Nagish, Inc. d/b/a Rylo", and the store seller is still Nagish Inc. (Play package com.talknagish.app). The App Store privacy policy link still points to nagish.com/privacy-policy, which redirects to rylo.com/legal/privacy. Language counts conflict (store 6, help centre 53 entries, website 50+, Desktop 60). Device requirements conflict (App Store iOS 16.6+, help centre iOS 15+). Rylo's help centre says the last 4 SSN digits are required, while the FCC FAQ says providers may accept other ID documents if a user has no SSN. Privacy messaging conflicts: marketing pages say Live Transcribe is 100% private and saved on the device, but the privacy policy says Rylo Live conversations may be recorded and stored, and the AI terms allow Live Transcribe input to be used for training. Whether Live Transcribe needs the full FCC registration (SSN etc.) is not stated; the help centre only says it is free for Rylo users. Speaker labels and translation for Live Transcribe are not stated. Google Play's Android version requirement was not visible in the fetched page. No 'Nagish Pro' or other paid plan was found on any current official page. The App Store lookup API returned no result for the UK, Canada, Germany, Australia and Slovenia storefronts; other countries were not checked. The FCC IP CTS consumer guide (fcc.gov/consumers/guides/internet-protocol-ip-captioned-telephone-service) returned 403 to WebFetch and was read in a browser instead; the facts here cite the FCC provider list and registration FAQ.
